subject: bitterling fish
title: This Fish Lays Its Eggs Inside a Living Mussel and Lets It Do the Work

scenes.text: This fish lays its eggs inside a living animal.
The European bitterling, a 3-inch minnow. Each spring the female grows a tube from her belly nearly as long as her body.
She finds a freshwater mussel, slides the tube into its breathing opening and shoots her eggs deep into its gills.
The male releases his sperm at the mussel's intake. The mussel breathes it in, and the eggs are fertilized inside it.
For about a month the embryos grow in there, shielded by the shell, bathed in the oxygen the mussel pumps for itself.
Then the fry swim out of its mouth. Some mussels squirt the eggs back out. The others raise someone else's children.

description:
The European bitterling lays its eggs inside a living freshwater mussel, and the mussel incubates them.
In spring the female grows a long ovipositor, inserts it into the mussel's exhalant siphon and deposits her eggs in the gill chamber. The male sheds sperm near the inhalant siphon so the mussel draws it in. The embryos develop inside the mussel for roughly a month before the fry leave. Mussels can fight back by ejecting eggs, and biologists treat the pair as a classic case of co-evolution.
Which animal outsources its parenting in the most shameless way?
first_comment: Bonus: the mussel has its own hitchhiking larvae that clamp onto passing fish, so this partnership runs both ways. Who is using whom here?
